messages:
raj_customer: Hey team — suddenly getting intermittent connection failures to our private inference endpoint in prod-vpc (10.0.12.45) since ~09:30 UTC. App logs show 'connection refused' and some requests succeed. No config changes on our side.

sara_support: Sorry about that, raj. Can you paste a minimal repro curl and any packet captures or VPC flow logs? Also which subnets/NACLs/NAT are in front of the Private nodes?

raj_customer: Repro from app host:

curl -v --resolve private.redwood.internal:443:10.0.12.45 https://private.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"test"}'

tcpdump excerpt:
```
12:31:10.123456 IP 10.2.5.12.52014 > 10.0.12.45.443: Flags [S], seq 123456789, win 64240
12:31:10.223567 IP 10.0.12.45.443 > 10.2.5.12.52014: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
12:31:12.400000 IP 10.2.5.12.52015 > 10.0.12.45.443: Flags [S], seq 223456789, win 64240
12:31:12.500100 IP 10.0.12.45.443 > 10.2.5.12.52015: Flags [S.], seq 99887766, ack 223456790, win 28960
```

Behavior is flaky — sometimes RST, sometimes SYN-ACK.

ivan_network: That pattern often means a stateless ACL/device is blocking return traffic to ephemeral client ports. What do your subnet NACLs look like and is there an AWS Network Firewall or inline IPS?

raj_customer: We have a managed Network Firewall in front of the private control plane. NACLs were based on an old template: inbound ALLOW 443,22; outbound ALLOW 80,443, DENY all else. We assumed the firewall would handle state.

sara_support: Key point: NACLs are stateless. If the client uses source port 52014, the incoming packet to that port must be explicitly allowed by the NACL inbound. Many teams only open ephemeral outbound and forget the inbound rule for ephemeral ranges.

ivan_network: Also check the Network Firewall config. If it uses stateless rules for performance or has aggressive TCP session timeouts for TLS, it can drop or reset flows mid-handshake or during streaming calls. Confirm whether the firewall is using stateful inspection for TLS and what the session timeout is.

mike_reliability: Another angle: if there's a NAT in the path (SNAT) it can rewrite source ports — you'll want to validate the actual source port observed by the Private node. If NAT is doing port reuse, intermittent SYN/RST could appear.

raj_customer: Quick check showed an old NACL rule explicitly denying 32768-35000 outbound (leftover). I'll patch NACL to allow 32768-65535 both in/out on the app subnets and test. Also asked firewall team to verify stateful TLS inspection and bump timeout >300s for streaming.

(8 minutes later)

raj_customer: Update — after allowing 32768-65535 both directions on the NACL the failures dropped dramatically. Streaming connections stay alive now. Looks like the NACL deny was the culprit.

sara_support: Nice, thanks for confirming. For best practice: allow ephemeral range both directions on subnet NACLs that host clients talking to Private endpoints, or rely on a stateful firewall that tracks TLS and has appropriate timeouts. Document both in your infra runbook.

mike_reliability: Adding note to private VPC runbook: "Ensure NACLs allow ephemeral client port range (32768-65535) both inbound and outbound for inference endpoints; confirm Network Firewall is stateful for TLS and session timeout covers streaming" :memo:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T10:05:00Z by infra-team completed in prod-vpc-1 :white_check_mark:

ivan_network: If you see any remaining RSTs after the NACL change, grab tcpdump + VPC flow logs and ping me; we can correlate and check for intermediate NAT/port translation. Glad this was an easy fix! :+1:
